$comment: The three games in `from-one-sentence/`, as data. These are NOT exhibits and they are deliberately in their own file rather than as rows in `exhibits.json`: an exhibit is bound by docs/GALLERY.md's line rule and § Scale and was built by somebody who could read this repository, and every one of these three was built in an empty directory by an agent that could not. `sentence` is the prompt that produced the game, verbatim and complete — it is the whole claim, so it is never trimmed to fit a layout. `defect` is a real, measured blemish left in the source on purpose; a record that hides its blemishes is not a record. `size` and `packages` come from `from-one-sentence/README.md`, which is where the provenance, the verification and the reason these keep their registry dependencies are written down. `params` is a query the game's OWN code reads — Before the Bell supports `?demo`, which places two stalls and opens a gate, so the embed opens on the game being played rather than on an untouched square. It is the game's parameter, not an edit to it, and nothing here may pass a parameter a game does not already implement. `lead` is the one the page opens on.

games.name: Before the Bell
games.sentence: a game where you place stalls and open gates to pull the crowd to your bakery before the market closes

games.name: Chime Path
games.sentence: a game where you hang chimes along a mountain path and tune each one, so the wind plays them in order as walkers pass
games.defect: five HUD nodes ship under the contrast floor, and the agent that drove a browser still missed them

games.name: Evenfall Orchard
games.sentence: a game where you plant an orchard and each evening choose to harvest or let it grow, and it keeps growing while the tab is closed
games.defect: one phase of its day is 84% one near-black color, which its author never saw
